g.text: Interview Question Map - LLM Inference Engineer
Companion to Study notes → Interview questions | topic cluster -> question card (scenario + key answer) -> key formulas | 3 system-design walkthroughs below
Card: [badge Qn] line 1 = production scenario, line 2 = key answer / number
Why a KV cache? 'Just recompute' proposal
T(T+1)/2 token-forwards -> T; cost = memory + BW
WORKED: Llama-3-8B, A100-80GB, how many 8K chats?
7B + 100K ctx on A100-40GB: MHA vs GQA-8
Which term of 2*L*B*T*H_kv*d_h*S does each lever hit?
S: FP8 | T: window | Hkv*dh: GQA/MLA | L: CLA | frag: paged
1M-token context promised on one 80 GB GPU
WORKED: decode TPOT lower bound, B=16 x 8K, A100
M_KV = 2 * L * B * T * H_kv * d_h * S
What is MQA, and what does it cost in quality?
H_kv 32 -> 1: KV /32 | Q diverse, K/V shared | 16 KiB/tok
Choose H_kv in {32,16,8,4,1} for a new 8B model
AI ~ Hq/Hkv: 1 / 4 / 32 vs ridge ~200 -> still mem-bound
Retrofit a 13B MHA model to GQA with no pretraining
K_g = mean(K_i in group); uptrain ~5% compute
repeat_kv shape bug: 4x more memory than expected
TP=16 on a model with 8 KV heads: KV capacity?
TP > H_kv => KV heads replicated: 40 KiB/tok/GPU, 2x total
decode AI ~ H_q/H_kv : MHA 1 | GQA-8 4 | MQA 32 (ridge ~200)
Llama-3-8B KV/tok: MHA 512 | GQA-8 128 | MQA 16 KiB
K_g = mean(K_i), uptrain ~5% ; TP > H_kv => replicate KV
WORKED: DeepSeek-V2 128K KV, MLA vs MHA
c_Q^T (W_UQ_i^T W_UK_i) c_KV_j ; W_UV folded into W_O
Why RoPE breaks MLA absorption; decoupled RoPE
R_{j-t} between W_UQ & W_UK -> split q^R, shared k^R (64)
MLA vs GQA-8 for a new 128K-context model
GQA: head sharing | MLA: low-rank latent (576 / token / layer)
decode ~ MQA w/ 576-dim head: AI ~ 242 FLOP/B ~ A100 ridge
joint SVD + partial RoPE: -92.19% KV, ~0.5% LongBench drop
absorb: c_Q^T (W_UQ_i^T W_UK_i) c_KV_j ; W_UV -> W_O
<R_m q, R_n k> = q^T R_{n-m} k ; theta_i = base^(-2i/d)
RoPE + KV cache: cache rotated K or raw K?
cache K after R_m; rotate only new q_t,k_t at offset t
RoPE wavelengths for d_h=128: shortest vs longest
8K -> 32K: Position Interpolation vs NTK vs YaRN
PI m/s | NTK base'=base*s^(d/(d-2)) ~ 40.9K | YaRN ramp
Gibberish after 40K tokens on a 32K-trained model
OOD low-freq angles m*theta_i -> fix: PI/NTK/YaRN or truncate
theta_i = base^(-2i/d) ; rotate pair i by m*theta_i
<R_m q, R_n k> = q^T R_{n-m} k (relative position)
PI: m/s ; NTK: base' = base*s^(d/(d-2)) ; code q*cos+rot_half(q)*sin
WORKED: 70B on 4xA100-80GB OOM at 32 x 8K chats
need 85.9 GB of 136.8 GB pool; reservation 32K -> only 12
Block size 16: per-block size & waste bound (Llama-3-8B)
block = 16 * 128 KiB = 2 MiB ; waste <= 15 tok = 1.875 MiB
How does decode find K/V scattered across blocks?
1000 tok -> 63 blocks ; kernel: table lookup + online softmax
n=4 parallel sampling / beam search: avoid copying prompt
shared blocks ref_count=4; copy-on-write only partial block
250 MiB shared vs 244 GiB | block-hash chain, LRU, isolation
KV pool full: preempt by swap or recompute?
swap: bytes/PCIe BW ; recompute: re-prefill T tokens
paging = better utilisation, NOT fewer bytes per token
vLLM OOM at startup vs under bursts: which flags?
k_cache[num_blocks, block_size, H_kv, d_h] per layer
35% GPU util on decode: halve the fleet?
memory-bound: tensor cores wait; check DRAM BW util
A100 -> H100 gave 2.2x not 3.2x; L40S regressed TPOT
AI=10: 5 vs 10 | AI=500: 250 vs 500 | A wins only if AI>1000
Batching helps GEMMs, not attention: why?
GEMM AI ~ B ; attention AI ~ Hq/Hkv (indep. of B)
Memory-bound vs compute-bound: pick the right fix
AI<ridge: FP8 KV, GQA, window | AI>ridge: tensor cores, FP8
GEMM AI ~ B ; attention AI ~ H_q/H_kv (independent of B)
FP8 KV: AI x2 ; window 128K->8K: bytes /16 ; A100->H100 BW x2.15
iteration-level scheduling: leave/join at every step
p99 TPOT spikes when a 32K prompt arrives
32K prefill ~1.7 s stall -> chunk 512 tok ~26 ms/step
prefill compute-bound | decode mem-bound | KV 1 GiB/8K ~21 ms
Double concurrency with FP8 KV: risks?
S 2->1: 320 -> 160 KiB/tok (70B); AI x2; check long-ctx
Hours-long streaming session: what to evict?
window W + 4 sinks: M ~ W ; 128K->8K = 16x fewer bytes
chunk 512 tok = 8.2 TFLOP ~ 26 ms @312T ; 32K prefill ~ 1.7 s
FP8 KV: S 2->1 = 2x capacity ; window+4 sinks: M ~ W
TTFT = queue + prefill ; TPOT = decode step
Design: TTFT < 2 s and TPOT < 50 ms under mixed load
measure -> chunked prefill -> prefix cache -> disaggregate
Design: cut GPU cost by 40% (ordered plan)
paged -> prefix cache -> FP8 KV -> spec. decode -> model
MLA + FP8 + hybrid (25% attention) - Level 3 retrain
Debug: p99 TPOT = 5x p50, nothing changed
preemption? long outlier? prefill chunks? throttling?
order: fit W -> fit KV -> TPOT -> throughput
goodput = requests meeting both TTFT and TPOT SLOs
External vs internal fragmentation vs duplication
5 GB free but no 4 GB hole | 18 tok -> 32 slots, 14 wasted
WORKED: 32K reservation vs 1.2K actual on A100-80GB
Grow KV without copying: 100-token prompt, 16-token blocks
7 blocks -> new block at token 113, then 129; 0 bytes copied
WORKED: block size 4 vs 16 vs 256 (waste vs table size)
Ref counts + copy-on-write: n=4 samples, 2,010-token prompt
126 blk x4 shared | CoW: 3 partial copies | 362 vs 1,112 MiB
FlashAttention vs PagedAttention: who raises concurrency?
10^10 scores avoided != KV smaller | M_KV has no kernel term
Admission control: 20 GB budget, 15 used, D has 8K prompt
Static vs continuous batching: A20, B500, C50, D1000 tokens
Pool full (A3 B2 C4, free 1 GB): swap or recompute?
swap 2 GB = 80 ms each way | recompute 15.3K tok ~ 1.0 s
WORKED: 95% vs 85% VRAM utilisation: who wins?
1M tokens over 4 GPUs: what does context parallelism fix?
Design: apply the 10-step framework to a 32K-token RAG service
85.9 GB vs 51.94 pool | fit KV, alloc, kernel, schedule
external: 2+3 GB free, no 4 GB hole | internal: 18 tok -> 32 slots, 14 wasted
32K reserve 4.295 GB -> 12 reqs ; paged 1.2K = 157.3 MB -> 330 reqs
grow: 7 blocks -> #113 -> #129, no copy | waste <= (P-1)*128 KiB
Read each flow left to right: symptom -> numbers -> diagnosis -> fix -> verify. Arithmetic matches the worked answers in interview_questions.md.
A. 70B chatbot OOMs at 32 concurrent 8K chats (Worked, 4xA100-80GB)
Takeaway: the OOM was an allocation-policy problem (worst-case reservation), not a capacity problem.
chunked prefill, admit by free KV
Takeaway: at 128K the KV cache, not the weights, sets concurrency; FP8 KV doubles it, MLA-class models multiply it.
C. Meet TTFT < 2 s and TPOT < 50 ms under mixed traffic
KV 1 GiB per 8K ctx ~ 21 ms at 50
Takeaway: prefill is compute-bound and decode is memory-bound; isolate them in time (chunking) or space (disaggregation).
